title: Intermittency Signatures in the Deformation of a Passive Droplet in Active Turbulence
abstract: We use fully resolved nematohydrodynamic simulations to study deformation statistics of a passive nematic droplet in two-dimensional extensile active-nematic turbulence. We find that the droplet aspect ratio serves as a scalar probe of the active bath. Its increments show heavy-tailed distributions with dependence on the time lag, scale-free burst statistics and multiscaling structure functions which establish temporal intermittency. While the mean deformation increases with activity, normalized intermittency is strongest at lower activity. This suggests slower and more coherent bath forcing. When compared with translational and forcing-side fluctuations, it reveals a hierarchy of intermittency: shape is more weakly intermittent than translation and active-stress fluctuations, consistent with filtering by interfacial restoring forces. Power spectra show an extended near-$1/ω$ regime for the maximal normal interface velocity, distinct from the steeper, approximately $1/ω^{2}$ spectrum of the interfacial active stress. Soft inclusions thus reveal how interfacial restoring forces convert active forcing into bursty, scale-rich deformation dynamics.
summary: This work simulates the deformation of a passive droplet within active nematic turbulence to characterize its fluctuation statistics. The research finds that the droplet exhibits strong temporal intermittency, which is most pronounced at low activity levels. By comparing the spectral signatures of deformation versus the driving forces, the authors demonstrate that interfacial restoring forces act as a nonlinear filter shaping the bursty dynamics.
main_problem: The study investigates whether fluctuations generated by active turbulence are effectively Gaussian or exhibit intermittency when a soft inclusion deforms within the turbulent flow.
main_result: Droplet deformation is strongly intermittent, with normalized intermittency being strongest at lower activity. The droplet acts as a nonlinear elastic filter, converting forcing into bursty, scale-rich dynamics.
method: The authors employed fully resolved nematohydrodynamic simulations to analyze the statistical properties of the droplet's aspect ratio increments and associated fluctuations.
model_or_system: The system models a passive nematic droplet embedded in two-dimensional extensile active-nematic turbulence, governed by Beris-Edwards Q-tensor hydrodynamics. The dynamics include standard viscous terms, an active stress term ($\sigma_A$), and interfacial tension forces ($f_I$).
key_observables: Aspect Ratio (AR(t)), increment statistics ($\Delta 	ext{AR}$), structure functions ($S_p(	au)$), waiting times ($W$) and burst sizes ($S$), and Power Spectral Density (PSD) of the normal interface velocity.
important_parameters: Activity parameter ($\zeta$), time lag ($	au$), and various moments $p$ for structure function analysis.
main_assumptions: The analysis uses a one-elastic-constant approximation and models the droplet using continuum hydrodynamics in 2D. The comparison reveals that interfacial restoring forces filter the fluctuations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate PDFs of aspect-ratio increments, CCDFs for waiting times and burst sizes showing power laws, structure functions vs lag ($	au$), and normalized PSDs comparing interface velocity to active stress forcing.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from setting up the nematohydrodynamic model (including active and interfacial stresses) to analyzing advanced statistical diagnostics like multiscaling, burst statistics, and spectral comparisons between deformation and forcing signals.
why_interesting: While focused on classical fluid dynamics, the analysis of non-Gaussianity, intermittency scaling laws, and filtering mechanisms ($\omega^{-1}$ vs $\omega^{-2}$) provides a rich framework for understanding energy dissipation and rare events in complex, non-equilibrium many-body systems relevant to quantum field theories or open quantum systems.
